paper_metadata.title: Effective design of a Co-Ni-Al-W-Ta-Ti alloy with high γ′ solvus temperature and microstructural stability using combined CALPHAD and experimental approaches

evidence.quote: Alloy design of a Co -Ni-Al-W-Ta-Ti senary alloy was performed through a CALPHAD (CALculation of PHAse Diagrams) approach coupled with experimental investigation, with aim to attain high γ′ solvus temperature, microstructural stability, as well as low density .

conditions.test_method: water displacement based on Archimedes principle

evidence.quote: The increase of the Al / W ratio effectively reduced the alloy density of the base alloy. As a result, t he densities of the alloys with higher Al / W ratio (B -series) are lower than those of most other Co-Al-W-base alloys (about 9 - 10 g cm-3, shown in Table 3) [1, 4, 11 -16] and even comparable to the 2nd generation single crystal Ni -base superalloys, such as CMSX-4 (8.70 g cm-3) [17].

evidence.quote: The experimental Tγ′-solvus of the present alloys are all above 1160 °C, and the highest one therein is above 1200 °C (alloy 30Ni -B), which is an appreciable increase over that of base alloy Co-7Al-8W-1Ta-4Ti (1131 °C) and most other typical Co -base superalloys (Table 3) [1, 4, 11 -16].

These alloys show superior mechanical properties at high temperature compared to conventional Co-base superalloys, which are only strengthened by solid solutioning and carbides.
